quiz.q: In Java, what does -7 % 2 evaluate to?
quiz.why: Java's remainder takes the sign of the left operand, so -7 % 2 is -1. That's why `n % 2 == 1` misses negative odd numbers.

quiz.q: For FizzBuzz-style checks, which condition should come first in the if-else chain?
quiz.why: The first true branch wins, so the most specific condition (divisible by both) must be checked first.

quiz.q: What is the value of 'D' - 'A' in Java?
quiz.why: Characters are numbers and letters are consecutive: 'A' is 65, 'D' is 68, so the difference is 3.

quiz.q: Which expression correctly tests a leap year?
quiz.why: Divisible by 400, or divisible by 4 but not by 100.

quiz.q: Why might `int volume = l * w * h` give a wrong answer for large sides?
options: The result can overflow an int
ints can't be multiplied three times
quiz.why: An int holds about ±2.1 billion. Larger products wrap around silently, so use long.

title: Loops, Repetition & Patterns
tagline: Do it once, then do it n times.

quiz.q: Which pair of operations extracts and then removes the last digit of n?
quiz.why: n % 10 is the last digit; n / 10 (integer division) drops it.

quiz.q: What should a running product start at?
quiz.why: Starting at 0 would make every product 0. 1 is the identity for multiplication.

quiz.q: In Python, which numbers does range(1, 5) produce?
quiz.why: range stops before the end value.

quiz.q: To test whether x is prime, the divisor loop can stop when…
quiz.why: If x has a divisor larger than √x, it must also have one smaller than √x.

quiz.q: For a centred pyramid with n rows, how many stars are in row i (1-based)?
quiz.why: Rows have 1, 3, 5, … stars: the odd numbers 2i − 1.

title: Recursive Thinking
tagline: Trust the smaller version of yourself.

quiz.q: What are the two required parts of every recursive function?
options: A base case and a step that makes the problem smaller
A global variable and a print
quiz.why: Without a base case it never stops; without shrinking it never reaches the base case.

quiz.q: What does this print for f(3)?  f(n): if n == 0 return; f(n-1); print(n)
quiz.why: Printing after the call means the deepest call (n = 1) prints first.

quiz.q: What error do you get when recursion never reaches its base case in Java?
quiz.why: Every call uses a stack frame; endless calls exhaust the stack.

quiz.q: Why is plain recursive fib(40) slow?
options: It recomputes the same values many times
quiz.why: The call tree repeats subproblems exponentially. Memoisation stores each answer once.

quiz.q: How many multiplications does fast power need for x^64 (roughly)?
quiz.why: Halving the exponent each time: 64 → 32 → 16 → 8 → 4 → 2 → 1.

title: Array Fundamentals
tagline: Boxes in a row, numbered from zero.

quiz.q: What is the last valid index of an array with length n?
quiz.why: Indexes start at 0, so they run from 0 to n − 1.

quiz.q: When finding the maximum, what is the safest starting value for `best`?
quiz.why: 0 fails when every element is negative. Starting from the first element always works.

quiz.q: To visit every pair (i, j) exactly once with i < j, the inner loop should start at…
quiz.why: Starting at i + 1 skips pairing an element with itself and avoids counting (j, i) again.

quiz.q: After rotating right by k, element at index i moves to…
quiz.why: Modulo wraps the index around the end of the array.

quiz.q: What's wrong with `grid = [[0] * 3] * 3` in Python?
options: It makes 3 references to the same row
quiz.why: Multiplying the outer list copies the reference, so changing one row changes all three.

title: Working with Strings
tagline: Characters are just numbers in disguise.

quiz.q: How should you compare two Strings for equal text in Java?
quiz.why: == compares object references; .equals compares the characters.

quiz.q: Why use StringBuilder instead of s = s + c inside a loop?
options: Strings are immutable, so + creates a new string every time
quiz.why: Each + copies the whole string, turning a linear loop into a quadratic one.

quiz.q: For lowercase letters, what does c - 'a' give?
quiz.why: 'a' maps to 0, 'b' to 1, … 'z' to 25: perfect for indexing an int[26].

quiz.q: Two strings are anagrams when…
options: They have the same first letter
Every character appears the same number of times in both
One is the reverse of the other
quiz.why: Same frequency of every character, which a frequency array checks in one pass each.

quiz.q: When adding two binary strings, where do you start?
quiz.why: Like grade-school addition: least significant digits first, carrying to the left.

quiz.q: You've been stuck for 10 minutes. What's the most useful next step?
options: Work a smaller example by hand
Add more print statements at random
quiz.why: A tiny worked example usually reveals the missing rule.

quiz.q: In base conversion, in which order do digits come out of the % / loop?
quiz.why: n % b gives the last digit first, so you prepend or reverse at the end.

quiz.q: Why does the Excel-title conversion subtract 1 from n each step?
options: Because columns have no zero digit (A=1 … Z=26)
quiz.why: Shifting 1..26 to 0..25 lets ordinary base-26 math work.

quiz.q: In spiral traversal, why check `top <= bottom` again before walking the bottom row?
options: So a single remaining row isn't printed twice
quiz.why: After moving top down, there may be no rows left; walking the bottom row would repeat elements.

quiz.q: Which edge cases should you test almost every time?
options: Empty / single element / all equal / largest values / negatives
quiz.why: These are where off-by-one, overflow and sign bugs hide.
